tests.description: A collection whose manifest owns citations: the clean page, the manifest column, a finding on the entry's line, the half-moved page, the writes, and the three refusals.

steps.description: The page's own frontmatter carries no citations: read alone, the key is unset.
With the config governing the run, the merged view carries the manifest's entry.
The check passes, and the row gains a fourth column naming the manifest and the entry's first line.
A finding about the entry itself is located on the manifest, on the entry's own line, and the page is what failed.
github annotates the manifest at that line, so the comment lands on the manifest's diff.
A page that still carries its own citations while a manifest owns the key is an error naming the manifest and the collection.

runShell.stdio: /"citations" is owned by manifest \S*citations\.yaml \(collection site\); remove it from the document/

steps.description: add writes the entry to the manifest, and the claim stays on the line that was typed, because the page is not touched.
update repairs two entries in one manifest and writes that manifest once.
A manifest keyed by a page field matches on that field, so the entry travels with the page rather than with its path.
Refusal one: a URL manifest cannot own citations, because cite writes them. Exit 2, before any page is read.

runShell.stdio: collection site: citations cannot come from a URL manifest, because cite writes them.

steps.description: Refusal two: a page in two collections whose manifests both own citations has no owner the tool can pick.

runShell.stdio: docs/page.md is in collections site and api, and both keep citations in a manifest.

steps.description: Refusal three: add from stdin has no path to key the manifest entry by.

runShell.command:
printf -- '---
title: T
---
# T

The fetch timeout is 10 seconds.
' | npx @hawkeyexl/manni cite add -:6 src/limits.ts:2 --as markdown --id t -c test/fixtures/cite-sidecar/manni.config.yaml
runShell.stdio: A page read from stdin has no path, and its citations live in
